title: Redwood PLG Quickstart - Discovery with Talos Analytics
summary: Introductory discovery for Redwood PLG quickstart. Customer evaluating Redwood hosted API for a self-serve flow, questions on free credits/time-to-first-token, and tradeoffs with Dedicated/Private deployments. Security and perf benchmarks requested; agreed to a short pilot and follow-up technical deep dive.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
next_steps: Redwood to send quickstart guide and free credits instructions
SE to share benchmark template and ask-for-data spreadsheet
Schedule technical deep dive to demo Dedicated and Private options next week
Customer to provision trial account and run TTF test with sample workload
action_items: Maya Chen: Send PLG quickstart doc + free credits link (due 2026-10-13)
Diego Alvarez: Share benchmark template & testing checklist (due 2026-10-14)
Samir Rao: Provide sample traffic profile and SLOs (due 2026-10-16)
Priya Patel: Set up pilot workspace and invite Talos users (due 2026-10-15)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Samir Rao: Hey Maya, Samir here, CTO at Talos. We've got Lena, Jules, Amit on the line.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Hi all, excited to dig in.
[00:15] Diego Alvarez: Diego from Redwood SE team, I'll do a little tech follow-up after the overview.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Great. Objective for today — understand your use case, make sure quickstart + free credits get you to first token fast, and flag any security or infra constraints.
[00:30] Amit Shah: Our main goal is to add a lightweight assistant into our analytics UI. PLG friendly flow — try in product, low friction sign-up, then convert. So quickstart and time-to-first-token matter.
[00:40] Maya Chen: Totally. Quick note: Redwood hosted API supports self-serve with free credits, SDKs in Python/JS, and a one-minute quickstart to first token in most cases.
[00:52] Jules Park: Can you clarify free credits? Are they tied to an account or org?
[00:58] Maya Chen: Good question — the quickstart credits are tied to the account you sign up with; they cover hosted API usage for dev/test. For Dedicated/Private we typically shift to a contract/reservation model, but we can set aside pilot capacity.
[01:12] Samir Rao: For us, data residency and audit logs are important. We're in EU region mostly. Do you have SOC2 and region controls?
[01:20] Diego Alvarez: Yes — Redwood has SOC2, support for region selection in hosted API, and audit logs. For stronger isolation we offer Dedicated and Private deployments with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS.
[01:34] Lena Ortiz: Curious about performance. If we embed assistant in our UI, tail-latency matters. How does hosted compare to Dedicated for latency/cost?
[01:45] Priya Patel: Short answer: hosted is fast for many bursty PLG scenarios, but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower P95 tail-latency for sustained high QPS. Cost tradeoff depends on your traffic profile — we can run a quick benchmark with your sample workload.
[02:03] Jules Park: Do you support continuous batching and KV cache? We have long-context prompts and want to reuse history across requests.
[02:10] Diego Alvarez: Yes — runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; batching is automatic where it helps, but we provide knobs in Redwood Optimize to tune batching vs latency.
[02:22] Amit Shah: What's the typical time-to-first-token if we follow the quickstart? We want to instrument in our CI.
[02:28] Maya Chen: From signup to first token often under 10 minutes if you use the SDK and sample prompts. If you hit any snags we'll escalate via support; we'll also provide a one-pager to instrument metrics.
[02:40] Lena Ortiz: Any gotchas around auth? We use Okta SSO and need SAML for org provisioning.
[02:46] Diego Alvarez: We integrate with SSO/SAML for enterprise orgs on hosted; for Dedicated/Private there's SAML + SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC.
[02:58] Samir Rao: On the topic of security: do you have customer-managed KMS and HSM support? We need to show encryption at rest keys are ours.
[03:06] Priya Patel: For Private deployments we support customer KMS integration and HSM options; for hosted we offer envelope encryption + key rotation and can discuss dedicated key options for enterprise customers.
[03:20] Jules Park: If we do a quick pilot on hosted, what level of telemetry and logs do we get? We need token-level cost breakdowns and latency per route.
[03:30] Diego Alvarez: The Console surfaces token-level cost, per-route latency, traces, and you can ingest traces to your observability system. For more retention we have an add-on.
[03:40] Amit Shah: Pricing — do you have a PLG per-token rate and then different pricing for Dedicated?
[03:46] Maya Chen: Yes, hosted is usage-based per-token; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits, and Private is enterprise license + support. We'll send pricing examples in follow-up.
[03:55] Lena Ortiz: We often evaluate models for tradeoffs — quantized variants, etc. How easy is model swapping?
[04:02] Diego Alvarez: The platform supports model pinning and automated fallback. Smart routing can route by latency/cost/region and we can do canary rollouts.
[04:12] Samir Rao: Ok — next we'd like a short pilot to validate latency and cost with our sample workload. We can provide a QPS profile and some sample prompts.
[04:20] Maya Chen: Perfect. Diego, we'll ask for the benchmark template.
[04:24] Diego Alvarez: I'll share a spreadsheet with workload template, SLOs to test, and a simple harness script to measure P95 and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:33] Jules Park: For the pilot, are there rate limits? We want to avoid throttling during tests.
[04:38] Priya Patel: For pilots we typically raise default limits; if you need dedicated throughput we can provision short-term Dedicated capacity or burst pool.
[04:46] Amit Shah: Any legal/procurement items to flag early? Data processing addendum?
[04:50] Maya Chen: We'll include our DPA and SOC2 report in the follow-up packet. For Dedicated/Private we have contract templates.
[04:58] Samir Rao: Great — action items?
[05:02] Maya Chen: Action items recap: we'll send quickstart doc + credits, Diego will send benchmark template, Priya will spin up pilot workspace. You (Samir) will send sample traffic profile and success criteria.
[05:15] Samir Rao: Sounds good. Also schedule a deeper technical session next week to look at Dedicated and Private setup.
[05:22] Maya Chen: I'll send a calendar invite for the technical deep dive. Diego, any final notes?
[05:27] Diego Alvarez: Just that if you want a one-click quickstart link I'll include that in the email; it includes SDK snippets and an example harness for TTF.
[05:36] Lena Ortiz: One last question — any known model compatibility issues with our long-context use case?
[05:40] Priya Patel: Not typically; we have quantized long-context variants and can recommend config. We'll validate in benchmark.
[05:48] Maya Chen: OK great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with docs and schedule the deep dive.
[05:55] Amit Shah: Thanks all.
[06:00] (call end)
